messages.text: I'm 68 and can't afford my Medicare costs. Can I get TennCare too?

I can help check that. I need a few details first.

1. Do you live alone, or does anyone live with you and share food? If so, how old are they?
2. What is your income each month before taxes? Please include Social Security, a pension, and any work income, and tell me where each one comes from.

If you know them, it also helps to tell me:
- Your monthly rent or mortgage.
- Whether you have a disability.
- Your monthly medical bills.

I live alone, no one else in the home. I'm 68.

My only income is Social Security, $1,250 a month. No pension, no work income.

Rent is $550 a month. Heating and cooling are separate from that. My out-of-pocket medical costs are about $180 a month.

Thanks, that helps. I have two quick questions before I give you the full picture:

1. Do you already get any of these: food assistance (SNAP), TennCare, or a Medicare Savings Program that helps pay your Medicare costs?
2. About how much do you have in cash and bank accounts? You can skip this if you'd rather not say.
No, I don't get any of those. Just Medicare. I have about $1,200 in savings.

**Food assistance (SNAP) looks likely, and a TennCare caseworker needs to look at your case.**

**TennCare (needs a caseworker)**
- I can't say yes or no for TennCare. People 65 and older are checked under different rules than younger adults. Those rules include limits on savings and other resources.
- TennCare Connect can check your case. Ask them whether you can get help with your Medicare costs.
- Apply at https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/ or call 855-259-0701.
- Source: [Division of TennCare, How Do I Apply for TennCare?](https://www.tn.gov/tenncare/members-applicants/how-do-i-apply-for-tenncare.html). The rule that age 65 and older is screened differently comes from [42 CFR 435.603](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-435.603).

**Food assistance (SNAP): likely, about $206 a month (an estimate)**
- You're over 60, so only the net income limit applies. Net income is what's left after the allowed deductions.
- Your income is $1,250 a month before taxes. After the standard deduction, your medical costs over $35, and your housing and heating/cooling costs, your net income is about $331. The limit for one person is $1,330.
- Your $1,200 in savings is well under the federal limit of $4,750.
- Sources: [USDA SNAP eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility), [USDA 2027 limits and deductions](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola), and [7 CFR 273.9 on medical deductions](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-273.9).
- The utility figure I used comes from older published numbers, because newer ones weren't available. Your final amount could differ a little.
- To apply, go to [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287.

**WIC** is for pregnant women, new mothers, babies, and children under 5, so it doesn't apply to you.

**Other help**
- Dial **211** for free local help with applying.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides who qualifies, and you can apply even if a screening says it's unlikely. Report your income and costs accurately on any application.
